*   Add up their signed shadow-volume contributions along grid columns to compute the voxel value [S1].

The claim states that the method computes the voxel value by clipping triangles at voxel boundaries, dividing intersections into sub-triangles, and adding up their signed shadow-volume contributions along grid columns. This is explicitly confirmed in Source [S1] notes ('Clip triangles at voxel boundaries, divide the intersections into sub-triangles, and add up their signed shadow-volume contributions along grid columns to compute the voxel value') and Source [S1] passages ('The algorithm clips triangles at voxel boundaries, divides the intersections into sub-triangles, and adds up their signed shadow-volume contributions along grid columns.') Both sources describe the exact same process.

Differentiable Voxelization via Smoothed Winding Numbers (DVX) is a method for voxelizing triangle meshes into smoothed winding number voxel grids that provides closed-form gradients with respect to mesh vertex positions, enabling gradient-based optimization of surface representations based on volumetric properties [S1].

The claim accurately summarizes the core methodology and capabilities described in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that the method (DVX) voxelizes triangle meshes into smoothed winding number voxel grids, provides closed-form gradients with respect to mesh vertex positions, and enables gradient-based optimization of surface representations based on volumetric properties. All specific details in the claim are present in the provided notes and passages.
supported
An optimization process that deforms a mesh to minimize the volume difference between the object and its extruded silhouettes from three orthogonal directions [S1].

The claim describes an optimization process that deforms a mesh to minimize the volume difference between the object and its extruded silhouettes from three orthogonal directions. Source [S1] explicitly states in the notes and passages that this specific method is used for making objects manufacturable by cutting with a bandsaw from three directions. The passages detail the steps: projecting the voxelized mesh along three orthogonal directions to obtain filled silhouettes, extruding them, and comparing the resulting cut shape with the voxelized mesh to compute the objective (minimizing volume difference). Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
